notes.note: The classic advertising aphorism, often attributed to John Wanamaker, is "Half the money I spend on advertising is wasted, and the trouble is I don't know which half" - not 5%. No traditional version of this saying uses a 5% figure.
notes.claim: There is an old aphorism in newspapers that states only 5% of your advertising is working, and you just don't know which 5%.
notes.context_quote: There's that old apherism in in newspapers, only 5% of your advertising is working. You just don't know which 5%.
notes.context_paragraph: And remember, you might get nothing out of stuff. It's just that you don't know what you get and one of the things might be nothing. There's that old apherism in in newspapers, only 5% of your advertising is working. You just don't know which 5%.

sources.quote: John Wanamaker once said, “I am convinced that about one-half the money I spend for advertising is wasted, but I have never been able to decide which half.”
sources.explanation: Confirms the traditional aphorism uses the figure of "one-half" (50%) rather than 5%.

sources.quote: The earliest match known to QI occurred within a 1919 speech... Half the money I spend on advertising is wasted, and the trouble is I don’t know which half.
sources.explanation: Provides the historical phrasing of the quote, showing no mention of a 5% figure.

sources.quote: “Half the money I spend on advertising is wasted; the trouble is I don’t know which half” is a classic statement on advertising, credited to both John Wanamaker (1838-1922) and Lord Leverhulme (1851-1925).
sources.explanation: Confirms the standard version of the maxim refers to "half" (50%).

sources.quote: “One half of their advertising appropriations are wasted” is recorded in print from at least 1897.
sources.explanation: Shows the historical usage of the 50% figure in this specific business truism.
